Goals and SLOs to Protect
-------------------------

- Availability SLA target to protect during cutover: 99.9% (monthly) for production routes.
- Immediate remediation thresholds (trigger escalation):
  - Error rate spike: sustained >5% errors for 5 minutes across tenant endpoints.
  - Latency spike: P95 latency >2000ms for 10 minutes.
  - Token cost anomaly: >200% of projected token spend in 30 minutes.
  - KV cache miss-rate >30% sustained for 15 minutes (for cache-sensitive workloads).

Pre-Cutover (T-72 to T-1 hours)
-------------------------------

1. Confirm stakeholders and channels
   - Primary CSM (Customer Success Manager): name + mobile number.
   - Tech lead (Customer): contact + escalation path.
   - Solution Engineer (SE): responsible for ingress, API contract verification.
   - Oncall SRE/Platform owner: PagerDuty schedule and runbook owner.
   - Slack channels: #cs-<customer>-go-live (private channel), #oncall-redwood, #se-ops.
2. Telemetry sanity checks — must pass before proceeding:
   - Synthetic journey (happy path) passes end-to-end: <customer> -> Redwood API -> response < 1s.
   - PromQL checks: error_rate/instance < 0.005 for 10m; p95_latency_query < 1500ms.
3. Canary plan and acceptance criteria
   - Canary traffic: route 1% of production for 30 minutes with zero critical errors.
   - Acceptance: no P0/P1 incidents during canary and no regression in model quality metrics (if applicable).
4. Whitelist and firewall confirmations
   - Verify ingress IP ranges, customer egress rules, and TLS client certs.

During Cutover (T0 to +4 hours) — Immediate Checklist
----------------------------------------------------

- Primary communications protocol:
  - All updates posted to #cs-<customer>-go-live every 10 minutes during the first hour, then every 30 minutes until stable.
  - The CSM posts customer-facing status updates; technical details posted to private channel only.
- Live monitoring dashboard (owner: Oncall SRE):
  - Tenant-specific dashboard showing throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, KV cache hits, token consumption.
- Escalation triggers (first responder must escalate within 5 minutes if triggered):
  1) P0: service unavailable for customer routes — immediate page to P1 oncall and notify Engineering Director.
  2) P1: sustained SLO breach (see thresholds above) — page SE and PM, start RCA and mitigation steps.
  3) P2: model quality regression detected — notify Applied ML and SE; consider traffic switch to verified model snapshot.

Escalation Ladder (contact order and responsibilities)
----------------------------------------------------

sections.section_path: Go Live Protocols Cross Org Communications Escalation 2027
sections.heading: Go Live Protocols Cross Org Communications Escalation 2027
sections.content:
| Level | Trigger example | Primary contact | Secondary contact | Action required |
|-------|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| L1 (CSM) | Customer questions, minor errors | CSM | SE | Acknowledge to customer within 15m, open internal thread |
| L2 (SRE) | Error rate >5% | Oncall SRE | SRE Lead | Execute diagnostics, apply mitigations (rate-limit, route switch) |
| L3 (SE/PM) | Persistent degradation >30m | Solutions Engineer | Product Manager | Coordinate config changes, model fallback, communicate to customer executives |
| L4 (Exec) | SLA breach or major incident | Head of Customer Success | Head of Engineering | Declare incident, engage legal/finance if SLA credits likely |

Note: The table above is intended as a quick reference. The full escalation paging list with phone numbers and PagerDuty IDs is stored in /confluence/people-ops/rosters and in the private channel pinned messages.

Common Mitigations (ordered by lowest customer impact first)
----------------------------------------------------------

- Increase routing to a higher-capacity pool (if Dedicated: burst pool)
- Apply tenant-level throttles to protect shared resources (quota reduce to 30% of projected steady-state)
- Enable model fallback: route to last-known-stable model snapshot
- Temporarily switch customer to hosted API endpoint (if allowed by contract)
- Quiesce long-running batch jobs from the customer side

Rollback and Safe-fail Strategies
--------------------------------

1. Safe rollback to previous routing config (SE executes):
   - Command: curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal.redwood/v1/route/revert -d '{"tenant":"<tenant-id>","to_config":"<previous-config-id>"}' 
   - Confirm routing table via: kubectl get svc ingress-<tenant> -o yaml (requires ops role)
2. Tenant quiesce API (customer-facing graceful shutdown):
   - POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/tenants/<tenant>/quiesce?actor=ops
   - Expected behavior: existing requests drain, new requests return 429 with Retry-After header.
3. Emergency switchback to hosted region: update DNS TTL and apply traffic policy TTL=30s for faster re-routing.

Communication Templates
-----------------------

- Customer-facing 1-line (acknowledge): "We are investigating increased latency for your production routes and will provide an update within 15 minutes. No action required from your side unless we ask."
- Customer-facing status update (10m cadence): include short bullet list: observed metric, action taken, owner, ETA for next update.
- Internal P0 page message sample:
  - "P0: <customer> production routes returning 503s since 08:12 UTC. Oncall SRE investigating. Initial hypothesis: ingress proxy thread exhaustion. Paging SRE Lead and SE. Next update in 5 minutes"

Telemetry checks / Queries (examples)
----------------------------------

- PromQL (errors): sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="<tenant>",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="<tenant>"}[5m])) > 0.05
- Token consumption anomaly (example):
  - Query: increase(token_count_total{tenant="<tenant>"}[30m]) / expected_token_rate > 2.0
- Synthetic validation command (curl):
  - curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"synthetic health check"}' | jq '.latency_ms'

Post-Cutover (T+4 to T+72 hours)
--------------------------------

- Stability window monitoring: SRE to keep watch for 72 hours; escalate on any SLO breach.
- Cost and quota reconciliation: Finance Ops and CSM to review token consumption, forecast delta, and apply quota protections if needed.
- Customer QBR prep: collect first-week metrics and any incident notes for the 30-day QBR.

-------------------------

sections.heading: Hosted Api Slos Enterprise Route Tiers > Error budgets > Error budget policy (what we do when we burn)
sections.content:
Error budget policy (what we do when we burn)

**Enterprise (Protected) routes**

- If burn is elevated, the default stance is **protect SLOs over throughput**.
- Allowed mitigations (in priority order):
  1) Tighten best-effort admission control thresholds (shed earlier)
  2) Temporarily reduce best-effort burst allowances
  3) Increase enterprise reserved capacity / pool weights (if available)
  4) Enable guarded fallback policies where contractually allowed
  5) As last resort: temporary enterprise throttling with exec/on-call approval and proactive comms

**Best-effort routes**

- Best-effort can be shed under pressure; we do not page purely on best-effort 429 shedding.
- If best-effort availability drops due to 5xx (not 429 overload-shed), we investigate as a normal reliability regression.

sections.heading: Sup 18477 Restore Fails Onprem Missing Crds
sections.content:

2025-02-19 13:44 PT — Customer (MedData Ops): Workaround succeeded after installing CRDs/operators first. Restore completed, but they noted the installer error message was generic and the runbook didn’t emphasize CRD prerequisites for a brand new cluster.

2025-02-20 12:11 PT — Customer (MedData Ops): Validation looks good. They asked Redwood to document "fresh cluster" prerequisites and add a preflight check that fails with specific missing CRDs listed.

sections.section_path: Pr 489 Add Restore Apply Workflow And Validation
sections.heading: Pr 489 Add Restore Apply Workflow And Validation
sections.content:
Pr 489 Add Restore Apply Workflow And Validation

Source type: github
Document ID: dsid_b8691ba2e29542838afae93928ad816a
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Add `restore apply` workflow with preflight checks and post-restore validation report

Implements the end-to-end restore path for Redwood Private in the installer CLI. This adds a new `restore apply` command that: (1) performs strict preflight checks (cluster connectivity, namespace/CRD readiness, version compatibility, storage backend access, and integrity checks on the backup artifact), (2) restores control-plane state in a deterministic order (cluster prerequisites, control-plane chart values/config, DB restore, then service rollout), and (3) runs post-restore health checks and emits a validation report that Support/SRE can use for escalation. The goal is to make restores repeatable, safer to run under time pressure, and easier to debug when something goes wrong. Restore ordering is intentionally conservative to avoid the on-prem issues we saw in SUP-18477 (missing CRDs/incorrect bootstrap order). Security note: we do not restore secret material from backups; we restore secret references and validate that required KMS/external secret providers are reachable. The report includes sanitized environment details (versions, timestamps, artifact IDs), step-by-step results, and pointers to relevant logs. Usage examples: `private-installer restore apply --artifact s3://<bucket>/backups/<id> --namespace redwood-private --report /tmp/restore-report.json` and `private-installer restore apply --artifact ./backup.tgz.enc --offline --validate-only`.

- Private installer: introduce `restore apply` with deterministic ordering, guardrails, and a support-ready validation report. - Adds optional `--validate-only` mode and clearer failure categorization (preflight/artifact/restore/validation).

response.query: Our Key Management Standard says we must not cache plaintext DEKs, but ADR-007 allows a short-lived in-memory DEK cache. What is the actual policy we should follow, and how should we describe DEK caching and KMS outage behavior in customer-facing rotation materials?

sections.section_path: Adr 007 Kms Client Wrapper And Failure Policy > Decision > Decision 5: Caching is allowed only for metadata and short-lived in-memory key material, with strict constraints > Allowed caches
sections.heading: Adr 007 Kms Client Wrapper And Failure Policy > Decision > Decision 5: Caching is allowed only for metadata and short-lived in-memory key material, with strict constraints > Allowed caches
sections.content:
Allowed caches

1) **Key metadata cache** (safe):

- Examples: alias → key ARN, key state, supported algorithms
- TTL default: 1 hour
- Negative cache TTL (not found): 60 seconds
- Must be invalidated on rotation/config change events where applicable.

2) **In-memory DEK/plaintext key material cache** (restricted):

- Allowed only for plaintext DEKs that are already present in memory for request processing.
- TTL default: 5 minutes (configurable downwards)
- Max entries: service-specific but must be bounded (default 10,000 entries) with LRU eviction.
- Scope: in-process only; never persisted; never shared cross-host.
- Must not include raw customer identifiers in cache keys (use hashed stable identifiers).
- Must be disable-able via config in regulated environments.

sections.section_path: Adr 008 Key Rotation Strategy Dual Read And Cutover > Proposed operational sequence (standard rotation) > Preconditions (all modes)
sections.heading: Adr 008 Key Rotation Strategy Dual Read And Cutover > Proposed operational sequence (standard rotation) > Preconditions (all modes)
sections.content:
Proposed operational sequence (standard rotation)

Preconditions (all modes)

- KMS integration uses the standardized wrapper and telemetry (ADR-007).
- Least-privilege IAM roles are in place, including separate principals for runtime decrypt vs rotation operations where applicable.
- Audit logging for key selection and rotation changes is enabled.

Sarah,

Following up from yesterday’s security review. Attached are:

1) A customer-facing KMS rotation FAQ (Private deployment)
2) A draft evidence checklist/template you can use for your audit/compliance evidence expectations (approvals, timestamps, change records)

Public docs (same content, web format):

- Private KMS integration: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/private/kms
- Key rotation procedure: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/security/key-rotation

Answers to the two items you called out on the call:
1) KMS outage / degradation behavior
Redwood treats customer KMS as a critical dependency. When KMS latency or error rates degrade, Redwood applies operational guardrails (timeouts, bounded retries with backoff/jitter, and circuit breaker/backpressure behavior) to prevent retry amplification and request storms. If KMS is unavailable for an operation that requires key unwrapping, Redwood fails fast and returns explicit errors rather than continuing with unclear correctness.

2) “Do you cache DEKs? If KMS is down, can you still decrypt?”
Redwood uses envelope encryption. Data is encrypted with a DEK, and the DEK is wrapped by a customer-managed KEK in your KMS/HSM. For active workloads, Redwood may retain short-lived in-memory cryptographic material to serve requests efficiently (e.g., within a process lifetime), but we do not rely on indefinite caching of KMS responses. If your KMS is unavailable, Redwood may be unable to unwrap DEKs for decrypt operations that require a KMS call.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call early next week if you want to walk through the rotation steps and evidence artifacts.

Best,
Naomi

response.query: Our Key Management Standard says we must not cache plaintext DEKs, but ADR-007 allows a short-lived in-memory DEK cache. What is the actual policy we should follow, and how should we describe DEK caching and KMS outage behavior in customer-facing rotation materials?

sections.section_path: Adr 007 Kms Client Wrapper And Failure Policy > Decision > Decision 5: Caching is allowed only for metadata and short-lived in-memory key material, with strict constraints > Allowed caches
sections.heading: Adr 007 Kms Client Wrapper And Failure Policy > Decision > Decision 5: Caching is allowed only for metadata and short-lived in-memory key material, with strict constraints > Allowed caches
sections.content:
Allowed caches

1) **Key metadata cache** (safe):

- Examples: alias → key ARN, key state, supported algorithms
- TTL default: 1 hour
- Negative cache TTL (not found): 60 seconds
- Must be invalidated on rotation/config change events where applicable.

2) **In-memory DEK/plaintext key material cache** (restricted):

- Allowed only for plaintext DEKs that are already present in memory for request processing.
- TTL default: 5 minutes (configurable downwards)
- Max entries: service-specific but must be bounded (default 10,000 entries) with LRU eviction.
- Scope: in-process only; never persisted; never shared cross-host.
- Must not include raw customer identifiers in cache keys (use hashed stable identifiers).
- Must be disable-able via config in regulated environments.

sections.content:

Preconditions (all modes)

- KMS integration uses the standardized wrapper and telemetry (ADR-007).
- Least-privilege IAM roles are in place, including separate principals for runtime decrypt vs rotation operations where applicable.
- Audit logging for key selection and rotation changes is enabled.

Sup 48271 Suggestions Savings Estimate Does Not Match Billing

Source type: jira
Document ID: dsid_85ee9562e05d457b9e32785343777359
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Optimization Suggestions: estimated savings does not match billing/usage totals (Arkadia Finance)

Customer reports that the Console > Optimize > Suggestions view shows an estimated savings that does not reconcile with their billing totals for the same time period.

Customer impact:

- Confusion / loss of trust in "estimated $/day" shown in Suggestions drawer.
- Customer is using this as input for internal finance review; needs a defensible reconciliation.

Customer statement (from ticket intake):

- "The Suggestions panel says caching will save ~$1,250/day for /v1/chat on Llama-3 70B. Our usage/billing only moved by ~$300/day after we enabled caching. Where is the rest of the savings?"

Environment:

- Org: Arkadia Finance (enterprise)
- Region: us-east
- Routes: /v1/chat (primary), /v1/embeddings (secondary)
- Models observed in screenshots: rw-llama-3-70b-instruct, rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct
- Suggestions feature flag: enabled (beta)
- Customer claims caching was enabled on 2026-02-19 ~17:00 ET

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Navigate to Console > Optimize > Suggestions
2) Filter to Project "prod-core" and Route "/v1/chat"
3) Open top caching suggestion (stable ID visible in drawer)
4) Note "Estimated savings ($/day)" and "Assumptions"
5) Compare to Billing > Invoices / Usage export for same days

Evidence / attachments (customer-provided):

- Screenshot 1: Suggestions list filtered to /v1/chat showing $/day estimate and risk badge
- Screenshot 2: Suggestion details drawer showing estimate range and stale_as_of
- Screenshot 3: Billing export excerpt with daily totals

Internal attachments (added by Support):

- Screenshot A: Console Usage Analytics "Inference cost (compute)" view (last 7 days)
- Screenshot B: Cost attribution query results for route/model (GPU-sec + tokens)

Notes:

- This is a beta feature; estimates are not contractual and use telemetry-derived assumptions.
- Need to confirm whether mismatch is due to time window, invoice vs compute cost basis, credits/discounts, partial rollout, or estimator bug.

1771741044 Beta Customer Feedback Estimates Seem Off

Source type: slack

Release: v1.0.0

support

Dev Patel: Heads up — early beta customer feedback: savings estimates in Suggestions look inflated vs what they see in billing. This is coming in via SUP-48271. Linking ticket: sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-48271-suggestions-savings-estimate-does-not-match-billing.json

Miguel Santos: yup, this is Arkadia Finance (beta). They said Console shows “~$1.2k/day (18%)” for a caching suggestion on their `/chat/completions` route, but their month-to-date costs don’t line up. They’re worried we’re “making up numbers”.

Supportbot: Ticket SUP-48271 updated by Miguel Santos (status: Investigating)

Marissa Cole: can someone paste the exact UI values (savings %, $/day, risk, confidence) + route/model? Want to see if this is a pricing assumption thing vs telemetry mismatch.

Miguel Santos: from ticket:

- Org: arkadia-finance
- Project: prod-vpc
- Route: `chat-prod` (their named route)
- Model: `rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct`
- Suggestion type: “Enable prefix cache”
- Estimated savings: `$1,214/day` (~18%)
- Latency impact: p50 +6ms, p95 +22ms
- Risk: Low
- Confidence: Medium

They also mentioned they already have some app-side caching.

Aditya Rao: thanks. first guess: estimator is using list price per token (hosted API) but Arkadia is on dedicated w/ committed rate card + blended GPU cost attribution. If we’re multiplying tokens by default price, we’ll overstate $.

Nadia Rahman: +1. Billing for Dedicated isn’t “per token list price”; it’s capacity + overage, and the cost attribution pipeline allocates by utilization. Suggestions estimator v0 currently uses `effective_token_price_usd` only when we have it, otherwise fallback to catalog price. Arkadia might be missing the effective price feed.

Logan Wright: checking telemetry: do we have the `cost_attribution.v2` aggregates for that org? If they’re on VPC/dedicated, sometimes the daily aggregates lag or are disabled depending on region.

Chloe Martin: I can look in optimize-suggestions service logs. Do we have the suggestion_id from the UI? (stable id should be in the drawer -> “Details” -> copy link)

Miguel Santos: from their screenshot URL in ticket (cropped, sorry) I can see `suggestion_id=opt_sug_01J3R8H9M7Y2KQ4...` (truncated). I asked them to copy the “Share suggestion” link.

Dylan Brooks: another angle: are we comparing against billing *after* discounts/credits? UI is showing “estimated compute savings” before discounts. Copy currently says “estimated savings” but doesn’t call out discounts/credits. Might be a perception gap.

Sana Farid: also, “already have some app-side caching” matters. Our baseline assumes Redwood cache hit rate is current observed `prefix_cache_hit_rate` (likely low if they’re not using Redwood cache). If they’re caching upstream, their request mix hitting Redwood may be different than what they think (e.g., they’re caching prompts but still sending lots of unique prompts to Redwood). Could go either way.

Dr. Maya Srinivasan: re: inflation — we’ve seen a bug in dogfood where we used *prompt tokens* for savings but billing uses *billed tokens* after prompt compression + retries accounted differently. If Arkadia has retries/timeouts, request-level token counts can be noisy.

sections.section_path: Pr 22044 Savings Estimator V0 For Batching And Caching
sections.heading: Pr 22044 Savings Estimator V0 For Batching And Caching
sections.content:
Pr 22044 Savings Estimator V0 For Batching And Caching

Source type: github
Document ID: dsid_fee94d81c032494cbfce8094468f0973
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Savings estimator v0 for batching + caching suggestions (cost + latency deltas)

Implements estimator v0 for the Optimize Suggestions beta (batching/caching only). Given a route/model aggregate window, the estimator outputs (a) estimated cost delta (USD/day + percent), (b) estimated latency deltas (p50/p95), and (c) confidence inputs that feed the risk scoring model (handled in a follow-up PR).

Motivation: The Console Suggestions view needs conservative, explainable estimates that are stable over time and can be recomputed on a schedule without per-request overhead.

Scope: (1) Savings model for two suggestion types: enable/raise continuous batching and enable prefix/KV caching, (2) assumption config + overrides, (3) unit tests + golden fixtures, (4) serialization to the suggestions record used by the Suggestions API.

Non-goals: quantization recommendations, per-tenant guaranteed savings, and automatic application. This PR does not change rollout behavior; it only computes estimates.

Implementation notes (high level): Estimator is implemented as a pure function over telemetry aggregates (qps, token in/out stats, baseline p50/p95, cache metrics when available) plus a bounded set of assumptions (token price, batch efficiency curve, cache hit uplift caps, and safety clamps). We bias toward under-estimating savings and over-estimating latency impact.

Key behaviors: - If telemetry is missing or sample size is below thresholds, estimator returns `insufficient_data` with reason codes (used by UI empty states). - Estimated savings are capped by `max_savings_pct` (default 35% for batching, 45% for caching) to avoid inflated outputs early in beta. - Latency deltas are computed as a function of concurrency + batch size proposal with a monotonic clamp so we never claim improved p95 from batching when baseline is already low-latency.

Config: Added `optimize.estimator.v0.*` config keys with sane defaults and per-env overrides. Assumptions are logged into the suggestion payload (for UI 'Assumptions' disclosure) but do not include any secret values.

Example output (illustrative): `estimated_savings_usd_per_day: 128.40`, `estimated_savings_pct: 0.18`, `latency_delta_ms_p50: +12`, `latency_delta_ms_p95: +48`, `confidence: medium`, `reasons: ["window_qps_ok", "seq_len_stable", "cache_hit_missing_using_prior"]`.

Testing: Unit tests cover: boundary conditions (low QPS, missing cache metrics), regression fixtures for representative workloads, and stability tests to ensure small telemetry changes don’t cause large estimate jumps. Added a small property-based test to validate clamps/monotonicity.

sections.section_path: Adr 015 Admission Control Layering Gateway Routing Runtime > Rationale > Avoiding feedback loops
sections.heading: Adr 015 Admission Control Layering Gateway Routing Runtime > Rationale > Avoiding feedback loops
sections.content:
Avoiding feedback loops

Layering introduces risks of control loops where:

- Gateway sheds → routing sees less traffic and declares healthy → gateway admits more → oscillation
- Runtime rejects → routing fails over → overload moves to another region → cascading rejection

We mitigate these via:

- **Hysteresis and smoothing** on saturation signals used by gateway and routing.
- **Single-step bounded fallback** (no multi-hop) and strict loop-prevention.
- **Separation of timescales** (runtime reacts fastest; gateway/routing react slower with stabilized aggregates).

sections.heading: Sup 2892 Fallback Model Not Triggering During Overload
sections.content:
2025-12-09 09:12 PT — Owen Phillips (Support): Customer (Banyan Search) reports fallback not triggering. They configured fallback from 70B -> 8B for overload, but still getting 503 OVERLOADED during peak. Provided correlation IDs and noted they are using streaming on /v1/chat/completions in us-east. Creating ticket and pulling in routing/SRE.
2025-12-09 09:28 PT — Dev Patel (Support readiness): Confirmed this aligns with multiple questions we’re getting since overload protection canary. Linking SUP-2860 as customer also mentioned missing Retry-After on a subset of responses.
2025-12-09 10:05 PT — Peter Holtz (Routing reliability): Looking at traces for rwcorr_01JEMNQZJ5J9P2G6E3R9K8V6M2 — request is being rejected at gateway admission (breaker open) with shed_reason=gateway_concurrency_cap before smart-routing service is called. So fallback cannot occur because routing is not invoked in this path. This matches ADR-015 layering behavior.
2025-12-09 10:19 PT — Peter Holtz (Routing reliability): Confirmed tenant policy has fallback configured, but current behavior: fallback is only evaluated on downstream overload signals (routing/runtime) and certain error codes. Gateway-level shedding is treated as terminal to stop retry storms and protect downstream. We need to align with Product whether we want optional 'fallback_when_breaker_open' semantics.
2025-12-09 10:42 PT — Nikhil Sharma (Product owner, Hosted API): For now, we should be explicit: fallback is best-effort and may not apply when admission control rejects early. However, for enterprise customers we can consider allowing fallback on gateway overload with strict guardrails (bounded retries, no loops, only within compatibility group). Please propose a safe tenant-scoped override if feasible.
2025-12-09 11:10 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE lead): +1. If we allow fallback on gateway overload, need to ensure we’re not just shifting load to the fallback pool and causing broader instability. Suggest: only allow if fallback targets a different capacity pool/priority class and enforce additional max_tokens cap under duress.
2025-12-10 08:55 PT — Elena Popov (Routing signals integration): Found second issue: in cases where routing is invoked (runtime returns overload), fallback was suppressed for Banyan because loop-prevention saw attempted_models already populated from a previous internal retry. There’s a bug: we’re persisting attempted_models across an internal redirect even when the first attempt never reached the model backend due to a fast-fail overload. That makes the router think it already tried the fallback and stops.
2025-12-10 09:30 PT — Ravi Menon (Fallback routing architect): Root cause seems twofold:
(1) Most failures happen pre-routing (gateway admission sheds) => fallback not possible.
(2) In the subset that reaches routing, a header bookkeeping issue causes loop-prevention to incorrectly block fallback.
Proposed fix: clear attempted_models when the failure is classified as 'admission_shed' vs 'model_attempted'. We can hotfix routing to only append attempted_models after a backend attempt is made.
2025-12-10 10:15 PT — Amara Diallo (Gateway middleware): Confirmed gateway emits overload classification as 'gateway_admission_shed' with reason codes concurrency_cap / token_bucket. It does not call routing service in this path. If we want fallback here, it needs a design change (admission would have to consult routing policy, or we let some fraction through to routing for fallback evaluation).

Miguel Santos: from ticket:

Aditya Rao: thanks. first guess: estimator is using list price per token (hosted API) but Arkadia is on dedicated w/ committed rate card + blended GPU cost attribution. If we’re multiplying tokens by default price, we’ll overstate $.

Suggestions estimator v0 currently uses `effective_token_price_usd` only when we have it, otherwise fallback to catalog price. Arkadia might be missing the effective price feed.

Logan Wright: checking telemetry: do we have the `cost_attribution.v2` aggregates for that org? If they’re on VPC/dedicated, sometimes the daily aggregates lag or are disabled depending on region.

Pr 22044 Savings Estimator V0 For Batching And Caching

Source type: github
Document ID: dsid_fee94d81c032494cbfce8094468f0973
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Savings estimator v0 for batching + caching suggestions (cost + latency deltas)

Implements estimator v0 for the Optimize Suggestions beta (batching/caching only). Given a route/model aggregate window, the estimator outputs (a) estimated cost delta (USD/day + percent), (b) estimated latency deltas (p50/p95), and (c) confidence inputs that feed the risk scoring model (handled in a follow-up PR).

Motivation: The Console Suggestions view needs conservative, explainable estimates that are stable over time and can be recomputed on a schedule without per-request overhead.

Scope: (1) Savings model for two suggestion types: enable/raise continuous batching and enable prefix/KV caching, (2) assumption config + overrides, (3) unit tests + golden fixtures, (4) serialization to the suggestions record used by the Suggestions API.

Non-goals: quantization recommendations, per-tenant guaranteed savings, and automatic application. This PR does not change rollout behavior; it only computes estimates.

Implementation notes (high level): Estimator is implemented as a pure function over telemetry aggregates (qps, token in/out stats, baseline p50/p95, cache metrics when available) plus a bounded set of assumptions (token price, batch efficiency curve, cache hit uplift caps, and safety clamps). We bias toward under-estimating savings and over-estimating latency impact.

Key behaviors: - If telemetry is missing or sample size is below thresholds, estimator returns `insufficient_data` with reason codes (used by UI empty states). - Estimated savings are capped by `max_savings_pct` (default 35% for batching, 45% for caching) to avoid inflated outputs early in beta. - Latency deltas are computed as a function of concurrency + batch size proposal with a monotonic clamp so we never claim improved p95 from batching when baseline is already low-latency.

Config: Added `optimize.estimator.v0.*` config keys with sane defaults and per-env overrides. Assumptions are logged into the suggestion payload (for UI 'Assumptions' disclosure) but do not include any secret values.

Example output (illustrative): `estimated_savings_usd_per_day: 128.40`, `estimated_savings_pct: 0.18`, `latency_delta_ms_p50: +12`, `latency_delta_ms_p95: +48`, `confidence: medium`, `reasons: ["window_qps_ok", "seq_len_stable", "cache_hit_missing_using_prior"]`.

Testing: Unit tests cover: boundary conditions (low QPS, missing cache metrics), regression fixtures for representative workloads, and stability tests to ensure small telemetry changes don’t cause large estimate jumps. Added a small property-based test to validate clamps/monotonicity.

sections.section_path: Adr 015 Admission Control Layering Gateway Routing Runtime > Rationale > Avoiding feedback loops
sections.heading: Adr 015 Admission Control Layering Gateway Routing Runtime > Rationale > Avoiding feedback loops
sections.content:
Avoiding feedback loops

Layering introduces risks of control loops where:

- Gateway sheds → routing sees less traffic and declares healthy → gateway admits more → oscillation
- Runtime rejects → routing fails over → overload moves to another region → cascading rejection

We mitigate these via:

- **Hysteresis and smoothing** on saturation signals used by gateway and routing.
- **Single-step bounded fallback** (no multi-hop) and strict loop-prevention.
- **Separation of timescales** (runtime reacts fastest; gateway/routing react slower with stabilized aggregates).

sections.section_path: Pr 19422 Fix Throughput Metric Double Counting Streaming
sections.heading: Pr 19422 Fix Throughput Metric Double Counting Streaming
sections.content:
Pr 19422 Fix Throughput Metric Double Counting Streaming

Source type: github
Document ID: dsid_4b2ac6984bdf4737a18520e158b04453
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Fix throughput metric double-counting for streaming responses

Problem: Dedicated throughput SLO reporting was overcounting tokens for streaming requests. We were incrementing `deployment_tokens_generated_total` per-stream chunk (delta tokens) and then incrementing again on stream completion using the final `usage.completion_tokens` value. For non-streaming, the completion-path increment is correct; for streaming, it results in ~2x token totals (shape/model dependent) and skews derived tokens/sec in the SLO evaluator + dashboards.

Customer/ops impact: This primarily affects Dedicated throughput SLO compliance tracking (tokens/sec floor) and internal saturation indicators. It also contributed to customer confusion when comparing Console throughput graphs vs request-level `usage` totals (see SUP-18510). Billing exports are not impacted (billing uses metering events, not the SLO throughput counters).

Fix: Make streaming accounting single-source-of-truth by only emitting token increments from the streaming path, and skipping the completion-path increment when `streaming=true`. Additionally, guard against duplicate “final chunk” emission by tracking `last_emitted_completion_tokens` on the stream session and only emitting positive deltas.

What changed: - `api-gateway`: adjust token accounting so the completion handler does not increment throughput counters for streaming requests; the counter is incremented only via the stream chunk emitter. - `telemetry`: add explicit `streaming` + `accounting_source` labels to aid debugging (chunk vs completion). - tests: add unit tests for streaming lifecycle (N chunks + final usage) asserting exact token totals; add regression test covering the previously failing scenario where both chunk deltas and final usage were emitted.

Rollout notes: This changes the magnitude of streaming throughput counters immediately on deploy (expected ~-50% for affected traffic). SRE/Obs have been pinged to annotate the Dedicated throughput SLO dashboard and ignore pre/post comparisons for 24h.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): 1) Backfill/annotation for SLO reports that span the deploy window (SRE to decide). 2) Consider moving all throughput SLO computations to request-level usage events once metering latency is acceptable.

sections.heading: Dedicated Throughput Slo Escalation > Purpose
sections.content:
Purpose

This playbook defines the end-to-end process for handling Dedicated **Throughput SLO** misses or suspected misses. It is designed for Customer Success (CS) and Support to:

- Triage quickly and consistently.
- Engage the correct on-call teams (SRE / Infra / Observability) at the right time.
- Communicate clearly with customers, including status updates and written summaries.
- Route service-credit / compensation requests through the correct approval path.

This page is **restricted** because it includes internal paging triggers and credit approval guidance.

---

sections.section_path: Usage Meter Audit 2026 02 Working Notes
sections.heading: Usage Meter Audit 2026 02 Working Notes
sections.content:
- Largest deltas concentrated in streaming + retry-heavy workloads.
- Embeddings batched fix creates visible downshift in billed units for affected endpoints (expected).
- Some “unexpected” upshifts tied to region dimension fill-in (previously dropped rows now counted).

Action items

- Aisha: add dashboard annotation when “dimension fill” fixes cause apparent billing increase (so Finance understands expected behavior).
- Emily: list accounts needing proactive comms if billed totals change materially post-fix (coordinate with Support/Sales).

Daily sanity checks we want (Finance POV)
(These are what we keep asking for; Eng is building dashboard/job + alerts)

- Drift: |sum(usage_events billed_tokens) - sum(billing_ledger billed_tokens)| / ledger <= threshold
- Duplicate usage events rate (by dedupe key)
- Null rate for required dimensions: account_id, model, region, endpoint, request_id/idempotency_key
- Freshness: P95 event available in recon export within X minutes; P99 within Y hours
- “Dropped rows” count in aggregation pipeline (rows failing schema validation)

Draft thresholds (proposed — needs PM-1842 sign-off)

- Drift paging: >1.0% for any top-20 account daily OR >0.3% platform-wide daily
- Duplicate rate paging: >0.05% daily
- Freshness paging: P99 > 6 hours
- Null required dims paging: >0.1% for any required dim

Month-end close policy notes (WIP)
Freeze window proposal

- Close month M at M+3 calendar days 23:59 UTC for usage event ingestion into ledger.
- Late events after freeze: record as “late adjustments” and post to next month unless material + approved for adjustment.

Need to document

- Evidence retained: snapshot of ledger totals, reconciliation export query outputs, variance explanations, approvals.
- Audit trail for meter changes: PR link + shadow billing diff report + Finance sign-off + effective date.

Customer-facing / legal language questions (capturing for Legal)

- Token definition: which tokenizer/version; what counts as prompt vs completion; tool call tokens.
- Retries: “We do not charge additional tokens for server-side retries/fallback” (if true) vs “we charge for tokens generated” (if partials count).
- Caching: how prefix cache reduces billed prompt tokens; whether cache-hit depends on exact match; transparency in reporting.
- Dispute window: timeframe and required evidence (usage export as source? invoice ledger as source?)
- Audit logs: ability to provide per-request usage records under NDA?

Notes from specific meetings (raw)
2026-02-05 (Finance + Eng) — discrepancy sampling

- We should sample at least 15 invoices: 5 self-serve, 5 sales-led, 5 dedicated.
- Priority: accounts with streaming >50% and high retry rate.
- Mei: recon export table will include billed_tokens vs raw_tokens; goal by mid-Feb.

2026-02-11 (Legal) — contract redlines pattern

- Customers pushing hard on “token counting fairness” and “no double charge for retries.”
- Michael: prefer explicit definitions + examples; avoid promising perfect alignment with third-party tokenizers if we can’t guarantee.

2026-02-19 (FP&A) — margin model inputs

- Rishi needs: region attribution correctness + cache-hit rate by model + effective batching factor.
- If region dimension was missing, margin model is wrong; we need to back-cast with corrected region if possible.

Next steps (as of 2026-02-27)

sections.heading: Usage Meter Audit 2026 02 Working Notes
sections.content:
- Largest deltas concentrated in streaming + retry-heavy workloads.
- Embeddings batched fix creates visible downshift in billed units for affected endpoints (expected).
- Some “unexpected” upshifts tied to region dimension fill-in (previously dropped rows now counted).

Action items

- Aisha: add dashboard annotation when “dimension fill” fixes cause apparent billing increase (so Finance understands expected behavior).
- Emily: list accounts needing proactive comms if billed totals change materially post-fix (coordinate with Support/Sales).

Daily sanity checks we want (Finance POV)
(These are what we keep asking for; Eng is building dashboard/job + alerts)

- Drift: |sum(usage_events billed_tokens) - sum(billing_ledger billed_tokens)| / ledger <= threshold
- Duplicate usage events rate (by dedupe key)
- Null rate for required dimensions: account_id, model, region, endpoint, request_id/idempotency_key
- Freshness: P95 event available in recon export within X minutes; P99 within Y hours
- “Dropped rows” count in aggregation pipeline (rows failing schema validation)

Draft thresholds (proposed — needs PM-1842 sign-off)

- Drift paging: >1.0% for any top-20 account daily OR >0.3% platform-wide daily
- Duplicate rate paging: >0.05% daily
- Freshness paging: P99 > 6 hours
- Null required dims paging: >0.1% for any required dim

Month-end close policy notes (WIP)
Freeze window proposal

- Close month M at M+3 calendar days 23:59 UTC for usage event ingestion into ledger.
- Late events after freeze: record as “late adjustments” and post to next month unless material + approved for adjustment.

Need to document

- Evidence retained: snapshot of ledger totals, reconciliation export query outputs, variance explanations, approvals.
- Audit trail for meter changes: PR link + shadow billing diff report + Finance sign-off + effective date.

Customer-facing / legal language questions (capturing for Legal)

- Token definition: which tokenizer/version; what counts as prompt vs completion; tool call tokens.
- Retries: “We do not charge additional tokens for server-side retries/fallback” (if true) vs “we charge for tokens generated” (if partials count).
- Caching: how prefix cache reduces billed prompt tokens; whether cache-hit depends on exact match; transparency in reporting.
- Dispute window: timeframe and required evidence (usage export as source? invoice ledger as source?)
- Audit logs: ability to provide per-request usage records under NDA?

Notes from specific meetings (raw)
2026-02-05 (Finance + Eng) — discrepancy sampling

- We should sample at least 15 invoices: 5 self-serve, 5 sales-led, 5 dedicated.
- Priority: accounts with streaming >50% and high retry rate.
- Mei: recon export table will include billed_tokens vs raw_tokens; goal by mid-Feb.

2026-02-11 (Legal) — contract redlines pattern

- Customers pushing hard on “token counting fairness” and “no double charge for retries.”
- Michael: prefer explicit definitions + examples; avoid promising perfect alignment with third-party tokenizers if we can’t guarantee.

2026-02-19 (FP&A) — margin model inputs

- Rishi needs: region attribution correctness + cache-hit rate by model + effective batching factor.
- If region dimension was missing, margin model is wrong; we need to back-cast with corrected region if possible.

Next steps (as of 2026-02-27)

Source type: gmail

Re: Trident Financial Services — DPA + SLA redlines (Private/VPC)

From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@tridentfs.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Mehra <raj.mehra@tridentfs.com>, Maya Chen <maya.chen@tridentfs.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, May 20, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Trident Financial Services — DPA + SLA redlines (Private/VPC)

Michael,

Attached are Trident’s redlines to (i) the DPA and (ii) the SLA. Key items called out in comments in the docs:

1) Data residency: require “no processing outside the United States” and restrictions on subcontractors.
2) Retention: require 0-day retention by default; deletion within 24 hours of request.
3) Audit logs: require export to Trident-controlled SIEM; log retention 7 years.
4) Security incident notice: 24-hour notification.
5) Liability: increase caps + remove carve-outs.
6) SLA: increase service credits; add RTO/RPO language.

Please confirm whether Redwood can agree to these as written, and if not, provide counter language.

Regards,
Elaine Porter
Senior Counsel, Technology
Trident Financial Services
Attachments:

- Trident_Redwood_DPA_Redlines_2025-05-19.docx
- Trident_Redwood_SLA_Redlines_2025-05-19.docx

To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, May 20, 2025 at 9:24 AM
Subject: Fwd: Trident Financial Services — DPA + SLA redlines (Private/VPC)

Fwd’ing Trident redlines. They’re pushing hard on “US-only processing” + long audit log retention. This is for Private (VPC) deployment.

We need a quick turnaround — procurement wants a same-week response.

Avery

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, May 20, 2025 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Trident — DPA/SLA redlines (need positions today)

Team — pls review Trident redlines (attached). Need positions + proposed counter language today.

Top risk flags / where we likely need to counter:
A) Data residency / “no processing outside US”

- We can generally commit to processing in the customer-selected region for Private/VPC, but need to be careful about support access, telemetry, and backups. We should avoid an absolute “no bytes ever leave US” statement.
- Ask: Naomi/Aisha — what can we safely say re: support systems and subprocessors? Any standard language for “support may access from outside but data remains in-region” vs “support access limited to US persons” etc.

B) Retention / deletion

- They want 0-day retention by default + deletion within 24 hours.
- Need to align with product realities: request logs / audit logs retention is configurable; but 0-day might break ops/troubleshooting.
- We can offer tight retention for request payloads and define audit logs separately (audit logs are not the same as prompts/responses).

C) Audit logs / 7-year retention + SIEM export requirement

- We can offer export hooks (customer-controlled destination) + sample schema, but 7-year retention in our systems is a commercial/compliance add-on question and probably “customer retains in their SIEM” rather than us.

D) Incident notice: 24 hours

sections.heading: Security Faq What We Do And Dont Say > Topic-by-topic guidance (Do / Don’t / Notes) > C) Data residency (where data is processed/stored)
sections.content:
C) Data residency (where data is processed/stored)

**Do say:**

- “Data residency depends on the selected deployment mode and region. We support region selection for applicable workloads and can discuss options for EU/US constraints.”
- “Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) provide the strongest residency control because the customer controls the network boundary and hosting environment (subject to the chosen architecture).”

**Don’t say:**

- “We guarantee all data stays in-country.” (Too absolute; depends on region, telemetry, and integrations.)
- “No data ever leaves the EU.” (Avoid absolutes; confirm actual data flows.)

**Notes / nuance to preserve:**

- Clarify *what* data the question refers to: customer content vs metadata/telemetry vs billing/support artifacts.
- If the prospect requests “EU-only support access,” escalate to Security/GRC and Legal (access controls + contractual terms).

- Freshness and completeness charts for the period
- Any incident annotations
- Query fingerprints (table/view names + snapshot timestamp)
- Final sign-off comment (RevRec + Eng)

Retention:

- Store evidence per retention policy; do not export raw request logs.

sections.heading: 1769014420 Eu Data Residency Objection Handling
sections.content:
1769014420 Eu Data Residency Objection Handling

Source type: slack
Document ID: dsid_b8f2f50607a0406f9733f2e9ba4281c8
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
sales

Hannah Schmitt: Need quick help on EU data residency objection. Prospect (EU bank) wants “EU-only processing + EU-only storage + no US access” for Hosted. What’s the approved phrasing + what do we *not* promise? @Olga Petrov @Daniel Carter @Marcus Lin

Lukas Meyer: +1, similar objection came up in EMEA last week. They’re asking if *anything* touches US systems (logs, support tooling, etc). Want to keep this clean.

Avery Johnson: Same here on another deal. Can we get a pasteable paragraph + a “don’t say this” list?

Priyom Das: They also asked if model routing could ever fail over to a non-EU region under load. Need to confirm.

Marcus Lin: jumping in. First: do NOT promise “EU-only” unless we’re talking Private deployment w/ customer-controlled infra, or we have a written contract amendment that explicitly defines what’s in/out.

Marcus Lin: For Hosted: we can support region selection (incl EU) for request processing, but we should be precise that some operational metadata may be processed/stored outside the selected region depending on the system (billing, abuse prevention, support). We need to use the approved language.

Naomi Feldman: +1. Also: don’t imply “no failover ever.” Our default is to keep traffic in-region if you’ve selected EU, but we can’t blanket guarantee “never leaves EU under any condition” unless it’s explicitly in the commercial terms / Private. Say “region-pinned” and “no cross-region routing by default for customer content” (but avoid absolute words like “never”).

Hannah Schmitt: got it. What’s the exact approved snippet? They’re literally asking for “contractual commitment that all data incl logs stays in EU and only EU staff can access.”

Olga Petrov: Here’s what we can say (approved style). Use “Customer Content” vs “data” to avoid ambiguity. Also do not commit on “EU-only personnel” access.

Olga Petrov: Pasteable response (Hosted + EU region):
“Redwood Inference supports regional processing for Hosted API workloads. When a customer selects an EU region, Customer Content (request prompts and model outputs) is processed in that region. Access to Customer Content is restricted to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis and is logged. Certain limited operational metadata (e.g., account and billing information, service health telemetry) may be processed or stored outside the selected region as part of operating and securing the service. For stricter residency requirements (including customer-managed networking and data boundary controls), Redwood offers Dedicated capacity in-region and Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments.”

Daniel Carter: + a compliance note: we should add “Details available under NDA / via the evidence request process.” Do not attach internal diagrams in email.

Daniel Carter: Also, for “contractual commitment” requests: route to Legal + GRC. We can say “We can evaluate specific contractual residency requirements; please share the questionnaire language.”

Lukas Meyer: Can we explicitly address the “failover” question? They’re worried about cross-region fallback.

sections.heading: Pr 4879 Publish Northwind Customer Story And Metrics Disclaimer
sections.content:
Docs: Added first public case study (Northwind Commerce) to /case-studies, including an approved quote block, architecture diagram, and a standardized metrics disclaimer component used across stories.

sections.section_path: Sup 3812 Northwind Dedicated Latency Spike During Interview Window
sections.heading: Sup 3812 Northwind Dedicated Latency Spike During Interview Window
sections.content:
Sup 3812 Northwind Dedicated Latency Spike During Interview Window

Source type: jira
Document ID: dsid_0c504258cd0c432d898e6711fb90eaf6
Release: v1.0.0
Benchmark: EnterpriseRAG-Bench synthetic upstream data
Northwind Commerce (Dedicated): transient p95 latency spike during case study measurement/interview window

Issue summary

- Northwind Commerce noticed an elevated p95 latency window on their Dedicated cluster while Marketing/SE were collecting performance numbers for a planned public case study.
- The spike was transient (~18 minutes) but would materially change any "single-window" p95 figure if captured during that interval.

Customer impact

- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions (streaming + non-streaming)
- Impact: p95 increased from baseline ~430–520ms to ~1.6–2.1s; p99 peaked ~3.8s.
- Error rate: no sustained 5xx increase; brief uptick in 429s due to queue protection (max in-flight).
- User-visible symptoms: slower first-token latency on some requests; a few retries observed by Northwind.

Context (why ticket was opened)

- This was surfaced during case study preparation (interview + metric capture). We need to:
  1) confirm whether the spike was a platform issue vs workload change,
  2) ensure mitigations prevent recurrence during future measurement windows,
  3) document the event so published metrics are measured over an appropriate window (e.g., 7–30 days) and/or exclude known maintenance events.

Timeline (UTC)

- 2025-10-09 16:42: Northwind reports "latency feels off" in Slack via CSM; SE flags risk to published p95.
- 16:46: Support opens SUP-3812; on-call begins triage.
- 16:50–17:08: p95 elevated; queue depth rises; autoscaler events noted.
- 17:10: Tail latency returns to baseline without customer changes.
- 17:35: Initial hypothesis shared with SE/Marketing; agree to avoid quoting that window.

Observability / dashboards

- Dedicated overview (Grafana): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/ded-nw/northwind-dedicated-overview?from=2025-10-09T16:30:00Z&to=2025-10-09T18:00:00Z
- API p95 by route (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/3xq-9qk-7eu/northwind-api-latency?from_ts=1760027400000&to_ts=1760032800000
- Scheduler queue depth: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/sched-q/scheduler-queue-depth?var=cluster=northwind-dedicated-us-east
- Node events (maintenance/drain): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/k8s-ev/k8s-events?var=namespace=nw-dedicated

What we checked

- Workload: No evidence of a step-function traffic increase from Northwind; request rate remained within typical burst bounds (+8% vs same weekday baseline).
- Model/version: No model rollout; pinned model version unchanged.
- Platform: K8s events showed a single GPU node drain/replace in the Dedicated pool coincident with the spike.

Investigation notes (most likely cause)

- Root cause: transient capacity reduction during a node drain (kernel security patch) combined with conservative surge settings for the deployment, leading to fewer ready replicas for ~10–15 minutes.
- Contributing factors:
  - Warm-up for the replacement node took longer than expected (image pull + cache warm), increasing request queue depth.
  - Autoscaler reacted, but scale-up lag (GPU provisioning) meant tail latency increased before capacity stabilized.

Mitigation applied

- Short-term (same day):
  - Increased min_replicas for Northwind Dedicated deployment from 6 -> 8 during business hours.
  - Adjusted pod disruption budget to reduce simultaneous unready capacity during drains.
  - Coordinated with Infra to pause non-urgent maintenance on Northwind’s Dedicated pool during the case study measurement week.
- Follow-up hardening:
  - Added an alert on "ready replicas < desired" + queue depth correlation for Dedicated clusters.
  - Documented recommended measurement window guidance for Marketing/SE: use rolling 7-day p95 (excluding maintenance/drain events) or present a range with a footnote.

Customer comms

sections.content:
Page 4: Evaluation best practices

**Proposed title:** “How to evaluate quality and latency before rollout”

**Customer-friendly guidance**

- Suggested evaluation approach:
  - Identify representative prompts (production samples + edge cases).
  - Run baseline vs profile-enabled comparisons.
  - Use A/B sampling (e.g., 1–5% traffic) with a rollback threshold.

- What to measure
  - Quality: task-specific metrics (pass@k, exact match, ranking metrics) + human review where appropriate.
  - Latency: p50/p95 decode latency and time-to-first-token.
  - Cost: cost/token and throughput.

- Rollout strategy
  1) Enable in staging on a non-critical route
  2) Canary in production (small % traffic)
  3) Expand gradually with monitoring

- Provide explicit “stop conditions”
  - Elevated fallback rate
  - Increased error rate
  - Statistically meaningful quality regression on a defined slice

**Note:** We cannot publish Redwood’s internal thresholds verbatim if they are considered sensitive, but we can publish recommended guardrails (e.g., “predefine acceptable deltas and require sign-off”). We will align with Selene Huang (quality guardrails) on what’s safe to disclose.

sections.section_path: Policy Engine Failover Extensions Draft
sections.heading: Policy Engine Failover Extensions Draft
sections.content:
- Decision must include:
  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)
  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)
  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.
  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1–3 alternatives and why they were not selected.

Proposed changes to policy engine
A) New predicates / functions
1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}

- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.

2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool

- True only if:
  - reachability.status == down
  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)
  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)

3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool

- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.
- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.

4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool

- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.
- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.

5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool

- Enforces ADR-042 “required corroboration signals” when configured.
- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.

6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool

- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.

7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool

- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).

8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool

- Enforces “can’t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval”.
- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.

B) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)

- Add an “evaluation_mode” field:
  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable
  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)
- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).

C) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)
Priority order (proposed canonical order for v1):
1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)
2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity
3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained
4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region
5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)

Notes:

- “No healthy fallback” means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.
- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include “degrade_allowed=true” hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).

D) Policy language / config schema additions
Add new fields (names tentative):

- failover:
  - enabled: boolean
  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]
  - signal_requirements:
    - primary_trigger: enum
    - corroboration: [enum]
    - min_confidence: float
    - max_staleness_seconds: int
  - dampening:
    - min_hold_down_seconds: int
    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)
  - safety:
    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)
    - max_flips_per_hour: int
    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int
    - rollback:
      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean
      - rollback_after_seconds: int
      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int

E) Output schema
Decision output (single object, JSON):

  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.
  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1–3 alternatives and why they were not selected.

Proposed changes to policy engine
A) New predicates / functions
1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}

- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.

2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool

- True only if:
  - reachability.status == down
  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)
  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)

3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool

- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.
- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.

4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool

- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.
- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.

5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool

- Enforces ADR-042 “required corroboration signals” when configured.
- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.

6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool

- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.

7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool

- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).

8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool

- Enforces “can’t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval”.
- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.

B) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)

- Add an “evaluation_mode” field:
  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable
  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)
- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).

C) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)
Priority order (proposed canonical order for v1):
1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)
2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity
3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained
4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region
5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)

Notes:

- “No healthy fallback” means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.
- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include “degrade_allowed=true” hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).

D) Policy language / config schema additions
Add new fields (names tentative):

- failover:
  - enabled: boolean
  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]
  - signal_requirements:
    - primary_trigger: enum
    - corroboration: [enum]
    - min_confidence: float
    - max_staleness_seconds: int
  - dampening:
    - min_hold_down_seconds: int
    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)
  - safety:
    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)
    - max_flips_per_hour: int
    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int
    - rollback:
      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean
      - rollback_after_seconds: int
      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int

E) Output schema
Decision output (single object, JSON):

sections.section_path: Sup 18477 Restore Fails Onprem Missing Crds
sections.heading: Sup 18477 Restore Fails Onprem Missing Crds
sections.content:
Notes: If the cluster has partially-applied CRs, delete the failed CRs before re-run to avoid immutable field conflicts.
2025-02-19 13:44 PT — Customer (MedData Ops): Workaround succeeded after installing CRDs/operators first. Restore completed, but they noted the installer error message was generic and the runbook didn’t emphasize CRD prerequisites for a brand new cluster.
2025-02-20 08:55 PT — Fatima Noor (Support): Requested customer confirm final validation checklist results (tenant config restored, routing policies present, control-plane endpoints healthy).
2025-02-20 12:11 PT — Customer (MedData Ops): Validation looks good. They asked Redwood to document "fresh cluster" prerequisites and add a preflight check that fails with specific missing CRDs listed.
2025-02-21 09:32 PT — Sean Gallagher (SRE): Logged follow-up requests for Eng: add explicit preflight CRD checks + improve ordering (CRDs before CRs). Referencing ongoing restore workflow improvements and helm hook work. Linking internal work to ENG-9822/ENG-9830/ENG-9828.
2025-02-22 10:05 PT — Fatima Noor (Support): Marking Resolved. Customer unblocked with documented workaround; awaiting doc patch in next runbook refresh.
Restore failure was due to missing prerequisite CRDs (cert-manager, external-secrets, Redwood platform CRDs) on a fresh on-prem cluster, causing "no matches for kind" during manifest apply. Workaround: install prerequisite charts/CRDs from the offline bundle first, then re-run `restore apply`. Follow-ups filed to improve restore preflight and documentation to explicitly cover fresh-cluster ordering.
Install prerequisite CRDs/operators from the offline bundle (cert-manager with installCRDs=true, external-secrets, then Redwood control-plane chart to install Redwood CRDs) before running `redwood-private restore apply`. If partial CRs were applied, delete failed CR objects prior to re-run to avoid conflicts.
Redwood will update the customer-facing restore runbook to add a "fresh cluster prerequisites" section and enhance installer preflight to list missing CRDs explicitly (targeting the next Private installer + docs release).
This ticket is consistent with recent restore drill feedback: restore should (a) detect missing CRDs and stop early with actionable output, and (b) optionally offer a "bootstrap prerequisites" step in air-gapped mode using bundle-contained CRD manifests. Coordinate with docs owner (Elliot Price / Kira Thompson) and control-plane eng (Ethan Park).

sections.section_path: Pr 489 Add Restore Apply Workflow And Validation
sections.heading: Pr 489 Add Restore Apply Workflow And Validation
sections.content: Ethan Park: The ordering looks good, but we need a hard stop if CRDs aren’t present. We cannot attempt to apply the control-plane chart before CRDs exist (this is what bit us on-prem). Also please ensure we fail fast with an actionable message (which CRD group/version is missing). Benji Okafor: Agreed—added a CRD preflight step that checks the required GVKs and prints the exact missing resources. Also added `--skip-crd-check` (hidden) for internal dev only; default is strict. Sean Gallagher: Can we make sure the report is something Support can ask customers to upload without leaking secrets? Also: step timings and error categories are key. Benji Okafor: Implemented redaction for env vars/flags that may contain tokens; report includes timings per step and `error_category` (preflight | artifact | restore | validation). Added `--report-redact-level=strict` defaulting to strict. Hanae Suzuki: Please confirm we never write decrypted artifact contents to disk in a temp dir by default. On air-gapped/offline this becomes a footgun. Also how do we handle KMS unavailability during restore? Benji Okafor: Updated decrypt path to stream to the restore consumer; temp files are only used if `--workdir` is set explicitly. For KMS: preflight checks reachability and key access; if KMS is down we fail before touching cluster state. Connor O'Brien: This should produce a stable artifact ID and include installer version/backup format version in the report. Also ensure exit codes are consistent for automation. Benji Okafor: Added `artifact_id`, `backup_format_version`, `installer_version`, and standardized exit codes (2=preflight, 3=artifact, 4=restore, 5=validation). Fatima Noor: On-prem edge case: missing CRDs after a cluster rebuild is common; the runbook expects the installer to provide a clear remediation step. Benji Okafor: Added remediation hints to the CRD check output and linked to the internal runbook section in the CLI message. Final review: Ethan approved after CRD check and exit code cleanup; Sean approved after report redaction review; Hanae approved after streaming decrypt change.

sections.section_path: 2025 05 28 Private Upgrades Technical Deep Dive
sections.heading: 2025 05 28 Private Upgrades Technical Deep Dive
sections.content:
[01:30] Fatima Noor: Sure. So the direction is: the installer generates an upgrade plan first, it’s a versioned artifact that lists stages and steps. Before doing anything, we run preflight checks—cluster health, storage headroom, DNS/TLS, RBAC, database connectivity, and also artifact availability. Then we orchestrate backups. After that we execute the plan in phases: control plane first, then data plane, with readiness gates. If something fails, we have deterministic rollback entry points that use stored state from the plan execution.

[02:05] Priya Raman: When you say installer—this is the redwood-private-installer CLI, right? Not Helm itself?

[02:10] Fatima Noor: Correct. Helm still does the actual apply of charts, but we wrap it with an orchestrator so we can be consistent and auditable.

[02:19] Marisol Chen: Auditable meaning we can show, like, exactly what checks ran and what was backed up?

[02:24] Fatima Noor: Exactly. Plan output persisted, precheck results, backup IDs, and upgrade start/stop events.

[02:31] Irene Choi: And timestamps, plus versions: current version, target version, and what artifacts were used.

[02:39] Marisol Chen: Okay.

[02:41] Markus Klein: Evan, can you describe your on-prem constraints? Like how air-gapped are we talking.

[02:47] Evan Wu: Fully. No outbound internet. We have an internal artifact mirror for container images and we can host a chart repo internally, but it’s manual. Also we need checksums for everything. Our security team won’t allow “curl random thing during upgrade.”

[03:06] Marisol Chen: And signatures if possible. Checksums alone are… better than nothing, but ideally there’s a signing chain.

[03:13] Fatima Noor: Yep. So we’re adding bundle verification: manifest, checksums, and optional signatures. The installer will fail early if the bundle doesn’t match.

[03:24] Priya Raman: Can it operate with, like, a USB drop? We sometimes do physical transfer to the restricted enclave.

[03:30] Fatima Noor: That’s a supported model. The bundle is basically a directory or tarball with a manifest file plus all referenced artifacts.

[03:40] Bruno Silva: And on the Terraform side for VPC it’s a bit different, but for on-prem we’ll document “offline registry endpoint” variables too, so the installer knows where to pull from without going to the public registry.

[03:54] Evan Wu: Okay. Biggest pain for us is, if Helm upgrade fails, we don’t know what state we’re in. Like, was the database migrated? Was it halfway? And then we get stuck.

[04:08] Sean Gallagher: Right. So we’re defining “rollback hooks” as part of the plan. The critical part is: schema migrations have to be guarded. We’re implementing idempotency checks and lock timeouts. Also, we’re biasing to backwards-compatible changes when possible so rollback doesn’t require “un-migrating” data.

[04:28] Jake Miller: That’s good in theory but we’ve seen migration jobs hold locks for a long time.

[04:32] Sean Gallagher: Yep. We’ve been tuning defaults—like statement timeouts and lock timeouts—so a bad migration doesn’t freeze the cluster. And the precheck will also test DB connectivity and maybe space.

[04:45] Priya Raman: Can we dig into prechecks? Which ones are blocking? Because we don’t want the system to block over something we accept risk on.

sections.heading: Security Faq What We Do And Dont Say > Topic-by-topic guidance (Do / Don’t / Notes) > J) “Air-gapped” / on-prem claims
sections.content:
J) “Air-gapped” / on-prem claims

**Do say:**

- “Redwood Private includes private deployment options; some customers deploy in isolated environments depending on architecture and requirements.”

**Don’t say:**

- “We support fully air-gapped deployments as a standard offering.” (Only state if explicitly validated for the specific deal.)
- “No external connectivity is required.” (Often untrue for updates, licensing, monitoring, support workflows.)

**Notes:**

- If a customer requires true air-gap, immediately escalate to Solutions Engineering + Product Security PM.

sections.section_path: Sup 18421 Enterprise 429 Spike After Priority Routing Rollout > Investigation notes (internal)
sections.heading: Sup 18421 Enterprise 429 Spike After Priority Routing Rollout > Investigation notes (internal)
sections.content:
Investigation notes (internal)

Hypothesis: us-east protected-route capacity protection enabled for Proxima allowlisted accounts; per-route/per-tier admission control is active and may be gating bursts more aggressively than intended for this customer’s contractual traffic shape.

Checks performed:

- Correlated spike with protection annotations in hot-route dashboard (SRE): overload protection activated for route-group "chat" + "embeddings" during a concurrent regional pressure event.
- Confirmed most 429s for this account carry reason=overload_protection_admission (not quota).
- Verified no corresponding 5xx spike; p99 latency for enterprise class remained within SLO during event, indicating protections are working for fleet health but customer’s burst profile is being clipped.

Open questions

- What is Proxima’s contracted peak/burst behavior (RPS and token/s) for these routes?
- Is Proxima being routed to a stricter per-route budget due to route-group defaults?

response.query: When a tenant has a fallback model configured, which overload conditions will trigger Smart Routing to attempt the fallback versus the gateway returning a terminal 503, and how should Support explain that behavior to customers?

sections.section_path: Sup 2892 Fallback Model Not Triggering During Overload
sections.heading: Sup 2892 Fallback Model Not Triggering During Overload
sections.content:
2025-12-09 09:12 PT — Owen Phillips (Support): Customer (Banyan Search) reports fallback not triggering. They configured fallback from 70B -> 8B for overload, but still getting 503 OVERLOADED during peak. Provided correlation IDs and noted they are using streaming on /v1/chat/completions in us-east. Creating ticket and pulling in routing/SRE.
2025-12-09 09:28 PT — Dev Patel (Support readiness): Confirmed this aligns with multiple questions we’re getting since overload protection canary. Linking SUP-2860 as customer also mentioned missing Retry-After on a subset of responses.
2025-12-09 10:05 PT — Peter Holtz (Routing reliability): Looking at traces for rwcorr_01JEMNQZJ5J9P2G6E3R9K8V6M2 — request is being rejected at gateway admission (breaker open) with shed_reason=gateway_concurrency_cap before smart-routing service is called. So fallback cannot occur because routing is not invoked in this path. This matches ADR-015 layering behavior.
2025-12-09 10:19 PT — Peter Holtz (Routing reliability): Confirmed tenant policy has fallback configured, but current behavior: fallback is only evaluated on downstream overload signals (routing/runtime) and certain error codes. Gateway-level shedding is treated as terminal to stop retry storms and protect downstream. We need to align with Product whether we want optional 'fallback_when_breaker_open' semantics.
2025-12-09 10:42 PT — Nikhil Sharma (Product owner, Hosted API): For now, we should be explicit: fallback is best-effort and may not apply when admission control rejects early. However, for enterprise customers we can consider allowing fallback on gateway overload with strict guardrails (bounded retries, no loops, only within compatibility group). Please propose a safe tenant-scoped override if feasible.
2025-12-09 11:10 PT — Rafael Mendes (SRE lead): +1. If we allow fallback on gateway overload, need to ensure we’re not just shifting load to the fallback pool and causing broader instability. - Action: Escalate if reproducible; include route + correlation IDs.

- Workaround: Customer can temporarily specify an alternate model/region explicitly (if acceptable) while we investigate.
- Action: Escalate; include tenant ID, configured fallback policy (what they intended), and correlation IDs.

sections.heading: Sup 18421 Enterprise 429 Spike After Priority Routing Rollout > Initial support response (guidance provided)
sections.content:
Initial support response (guidance provided)

- Confirmed that the new system returns distinct reason codes and customers should key their retry/backoff behavior on:
  - "quota_exceeded" (respect quota windows; reduce steady-state rate)
  - "overload_protection_admission" (transient overload; respect Retry-After; use exponential backoff + jitter)
- Recommended changes:
  - Use exponential backoff with full jitter; cap concurrency; do not retry immediately.
  - Honor Retry-After; treat 429 as a signal to shed load client-side.

sections.section_path: Adr 015 Admission Control Layering Gateway Routing Runtime > Decision > 2) Routing admission + fallback (secondary protection and graceful degradation)
sections.heading: Adr 015 Admission Control Layering Gateway Routing Runtime > Decision > 2) Routing admission + fallback (secondary protection and graceful degradation)
sections.content:
2) Routing admission + fallback (secondary protection and graceful degradation)

**Routing owns “where it goes”** and **controlled degradation**, not global rate limiting.

Routing responsibilities:

- Choose region/model deployment target using policy (latency/cost/availability) and health signals.
- If gateway-admitted traffic hits a saturated target, routing may:
  - Attempt **configured fallback model/region** (bounded, loop-safe) when policy allows.
  - Otherwise, return an overload response consistent with ADR-014.

Routing must not create uncontrolled amplification (e.g., fan-out retries across regions). Routing is permitted to do **at most one** fallback attempt per request, and must enforce loop-prevention.
